core_obligations: Reduction (proof lines 3664-3671): a bounded separable extension produces a rational point, after which the remaining bound is (n^{2g})!.
Torsion descent (proof lines 3673-3683): the standard torsion group over the algebraic closure descends to the separable closure by the Picard-scheme torsion lemma.

Galois bound (proof lines 3684-3692): the continuous action of Gal(k^{sep}/k) on the n-torsion has open kernel, so its fixed field k' is finite over k; Galois theory identifies Gal(k'/k) with the image inside the permutation group of a set of size n^{2g}, giving [k' : k] <= (n^{2g})!, and X_{k'} keeps its rational point with Pic(X_{k'})[n] of rank 2g.

Genus 1 (proof lines 3693-3695): the same argument applies once a rational point is reached over some finite separable extension (existence by the smooth-variety lemma); the author remarks that no uniform degree bound is claimed in this case (detail omitted on that auxiliary remark).
proof_roadmap: Move to a rational point over a bounded separable extension.
Descend the standard n-torsion group from the algebraic to the separable closure.
Bound the fixed field of the Galois action kernel via continuity and the permutation-group cardinality.
Handle genus 1 by the same Galois argument after obtaining a rational point.
difficulty_reason: The lemma makes the n-torsion of Picard visible over a finite separable extension with explicit degree bounds (statement lines 3642-3660). The proof (lines 3662-3695) chains: rational point over a bounded extension, torsion descent to k^{sep}, the continuous Galois action with open kernel, and the factorial degree bound from the permutation group cardinality; genus 1 reuses the same argument after existence of a rational point. The single omitted detail concerns the auxiliary remark that no uniform bound exists for g = 1, not the lemma's conclusions. H3: the Galois-descent orchestration with the quantitative bound is a genuine arithmetic argument.
